questions.question: Given the symptoms — content overflowing, a modal behind a header, a sticky that won't stick — what's the CSS scenario playbook?
questions.title: Css Scenario Playbook
questions.direct_answer: The four classic scenario families with first-moves: (1) OVERFLOW (horizontal scrollbar / clipped content): find the widest box with outline: 1px solid red on *; the usual suspects — 100vw (includes scrollbar — use width: 100%), a flex/grid child refusing to shrink (min-width: 0 / min-height: 0), unbreakable long words (overflow-wrap: anywhere), fixed widths on small screens (min()/clamp()). (2) Z-INDEX/STACKING ('modal behind header'): z-index only works on positioned/flex/grid items, and EVERY positioned+z-index ancestor + transform/filter/opacity creates a NEW stacking context — a z-index: 9999 child cannot escape its parent's z-index: 1 context; fix the PARENT's z-index, not the child's. (3) STICKY NOT STICKING: missing top/bottom offset; parent has no room; a mid-ancestor with overflow: hidden/auto changed the scroll container; or the sticky element is display: table-cell family. (4) SPACING COLLAPSE ('my margins vanished'): vertical margin COLLAPSE between adjacent siblings/parent-first-child (the larger wins); flex/grid containers NEVER collapse — or padding/border prevent it.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SYM{symptom} -->|horizontal scroll| O[outline all → widest box]
    O --> O1[100vw → width 100%]
    O --> O2[flex grid child → min-width 0]
    O --> O3[unbreakable text → overflow-wrap anywhere]
    SYM -->|element under another| Z[z-index ignored?]
    Z --> Z1[not positioned or flex/grid item]
    Z --> Z2[inside a lower stacking context → raise the PARENT]
    SYM -->|sticky won't stick| S[offset? roomy parent? overflow ancestor?]
    SYM -->|margins vanish| M[sibling vertical collapse — flex/grid parent or gap]
    PRF[outline over border — layout untouched]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The stacking context creation list (the deep knowledge — say the LIST and you win the round): a new stacking context is created by: root element; position absolute/relative with z-index ≠ auto; position fixed/sticky (always, regardless of z-index); flex/grid ITEMS with z-index ≠ auto; opacity < 1; transform, filter, backdrop-filter, perspective, clip-path; will-change with a context-creating value; isolation: isolate (the explicit intent form — create a context WITHOUT any visual effect, the modern 'contain my z-index wars' tool); contain: paint. The DIAGNOSTIC move: DevTools' Layers/3D view, or walk ancestors checking computed transform/opacity/z-index+position — the first context ancestor above the two feuding elements is where the fix lives.

The overflow diagnosis, precise (what outline tells you): horizontal scroll means SOME box's scrollWidth > clientWidth on the path to the viewport — outline everything, scroll, and the first box extending past the viewport is the culprit; then WHICH cause (fixed width vs min-content vs 100vw) decides the fix. min-width: 0 is the most-quoted one because flex/grid items default to min-width: auto = min-content — a long URL or unbreakable code string keeps the item at min-content width and overflows the track; the grid form is minmax(0, 1fr) (the '1fr isn't enough' fix).

Margin collapse, the full rules (the three collapse cases): ADJACENT siblings (the common one); PARENT with no border/padding/inline content separating it from its FIRST/LAST child (the parent's margin collapses WITH the child's — the 'why does the parent move' classic); and EMPTY blocks (their own top/bottom margins collapse). What NEVER collapses: horizontal margins; flex/grid containers' children; absolutely positioned elements; elements with a new block formatting context (overflow: hidden/auto, display: flow-root — the explicit context-creating fix: display: flow-root on the parent, the cleanest uncollapse without side effects). Modern layouts dodge the whole class by using gap.
